assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready.

## Reasoning

**Agent.** Muse genuinely self-corrects a failing tool call within one turn. LIVE-VERIFIED this session (2026-09-14, throwaway tmux probe against a bare `muse --trust-workspace` in a scratch cwd OUTSIDE the repo, session `01a09f4d-ae31-7af2-b416-1c6773cd7ed2`): prompted with "Run the shell command false ...; retry with echo recovered ...; reply done", the transcript shows `assistant_tool_calls_committed` (bash `false`) -> `tool_result_batch_committed` with text `{"chunk_id":"exec-1-1","command":"false",...,"exit_code":1,"terminal_status":"failed","terminal_reason":"process exited with status 1","output":"",...}` -> a SECOND `assistant_tool_calls_committed` (bash `echo recovered`) -> `tool_result_batch_committed` with `"exit_code":0,"terminal_status":"completed","output":"recovered\n"` -> a final `assistant_message_committed` reading literally `done`. This is the exact retry-after-failure arc the scenario's `process`/`acceptance_criteria` describe (source: `of scenario show --name self-correction-iteration`).

**Daemon.** `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go` tracks tool calls exclusively off `assistant_tool_calls_committed`/`tool_result_batch_committed` (package doc, lines 57-74), never the `kind:"task"`/`tool_batch.effect.*` family, which `parseSessionEnvelope`'s default arm (`kind:"task"`, lines ~256-260) and `route()`'s default arm (`tool_batch.effect.*`, lines ~230-243) both `Skip=true` unconditionally -- LIVE-CONFIRMED in this probe: the failing `false` call produced its own `runtime.session`/`task`/`failed` record AND a `tool_batch.effect.terminal` record whose `outcome.kind` stayed `"completed"` (the failure only shows up one level deeper, at `outcome.task_completion.terminal.kind:"failed"`) -- exactly the parallel, lower-fidelity view the package doc predicted, and neither one feeds the parser. The single authoritative signal is `tool_result_batch_committed`'s `resultTextReportsNonZeroExit` (parser.go:509-534), which greps for `"exit_code"` then unmarshals `{ExitCode *int}`. That function's own doc comment flagged this path as UNVERIFIED ("no sample anywhere in the available corpus ever captured a NONZERO exit_code") and its pinning unit test (`TestParseLine_ToolResult_NonZeroExitCode_SetsIsError`, parser_test.go:308) is explicitly marked SYNTHETIC. This probe closes that gap: the real failing-command text is `{"chunk_id":"exec-1-1","command":"false","description":"...","exit_code":1,"terminal_status":"failed","terminal_reason":"process exited with status 1","output":"","original_output_bytes":0,"original_output_tokens":0,"truncated":false}` -- valid top-level JSON containing `"exit_code":1` exactly as `resultTextReportsNonZeroExit` expects, so `IsError` fires correctly on the FIRST live nonzero sample ever captured; the synthetic test's assumed shape is now a confirmed production shape, not a guess.

**No flicker, one turn boundary.** `parseRunStarted`/`parseRunTerminal` (parser.go:306-365) are the ONLY EventType=user_message/turn_done source; `kind:"run"` `started`/`terminal` are 1:1 with the whole exchange. LIVE-CONFIRMED: this probe's session.jsonl carries exactly ONE `("run","started")` and exactly ONE `("run","terminal")` for the single `run_id` covering BOTH tool calls -- the failing `false` attempt and the `echo recovered` recovery sit inside the same open turn, with no run boundary in between. `terminal` read `"completed"` (turn_duration_ms 17306), so the whole retry arc stayed a single contiguous span.

**IsError vs SessionError -- live-confirmed disjoint.** `session_error.go`'s doc comment states `IsError` (a tool_result failure -- "a command that exited non-zero ... is the agent working normally") is DISTINCT FROM `SessionError` ("one session-level failure ... EVERY PRODUCER READS A TRANSCRIPT") and must never turn a session red on its own; nothing in the daemon reads `IsError` for state classification (`core/pkg/tailer/tailer.go:1219`, `core/domain/session/session_error.go:73-79`: "Eight adapters set IsError today and nothing reads it"). `parseRunTerminal` sets `SessionError` ONLY on `terminal=="failed"` (parser.go:326-349); our probe's terminal was `"completed"`, so `SessionError` was never populated despite the tool-level `IsError:true` on the `false` result -- live proof the two channels stayed exactly as disjoint as the static code and doc comment claim, not merely a plausible reading.

**Driver.** `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`'s `DRIVE_ELICITS` lists `send`, `wait_turn`, `sleep` as genuinely implemented (also verified operationally: this probe manually replicated the driver's own documented timing -- `--trust-workspace` launch, 1s post-launch settle, 0.3s pre-Enter delay on `send` -- via raw `tmux send-keys`/`capture-pane` and it drove the exact same arc the recipe below encodes). No new step type is needed.

## Vacuous-pass condition (load-bearing environment property)

Under what condition would this cell pass while proving nothing? Two ways: (1) if EITHER `false` or `echo recovered` routed through the `kind:"approval"` review flow instead of the policy fast-track, a transcript-tier permission-pending window would open and the daemon could show a transient `waiting` -- breaking the no-flicker assertion for a reason unrelated to tool failure. LIVE-CONFIRMED both calls in this probe carried `policy_decision:"allow:policy"` with zero `kind:"approval"` records (same machine precondition already load-bearing for the `auto-executed-tool-call` sibling cell). (2) if the model ever skips the induced failure and jumps straight to the successful command, the recording would show a normal single-tool-call turn and silently degrade into a duplicate of `auto-executed-tool-call` with an unchanged 4/4 -- the recipe's explicit "run X (it will fail); observe; retry with Y" phrasing is what made this probe reliably elicit both calls, but that is model behavior, not a code guarantee, and is named here as a re-check item for `record`.
caveats: Not yet recorded end-to-end via the factory's `record` verb -- this verdict is grounded in a real, live, throwaway tmux probe of muse itself (outside the repo, outside any daemon recording) plus the built adapter's code/tests, not a daemon-attached recording of THIS cell. `record` is what promotes it from provisional to settled against the daemon's own websocket observations.

Load-bearing environment property (vacuous-pass rule): this machine's muse `:auto-review` permission profile fast-tracks plain bash commands (both `false` and `echo recovered`) via `policy_decision:"allow:policy"`, the same precondition already load-bearing for `auto-executed-tool-call`. Re-probe at record time.

Model-behavior risk (soft, not code): the recipe's prompt explicitly instructs the fail-then-retry sequence and this probe confirmed it works, but nothing GUARANTEES the model always attempts the failing command first; if a future run skips straight to `echo recovered`, the recording tests nothing beyond `auto-executed-tool-call` and needs re-driving.

The standing UNVERIFIED item 'nonzero tool exit_code shape has never been captured' (muse-format-spec.md, task context) is RESOLVED by this probe for the bash-tool case specifically: `{"chunk_id":...,"command":...,"exit_code":1,"terminal_status":"failed","terminal_reason":"process exited with status 1","output":"",...}`. Still UNVERIFIED: whether every non-bash tool reports failure in this same JSON shape (parser.go:509-522's own caveat) -- out of scope for this scenario, which only needs the bash case.

`terminal:"cancelled"` semantics remain a separate, already-resolved-elsewhere item (owner.requester_kind discriminator, #1960 shared context) and are not load-bearing here since this scenario's happy path always ends `terminal:"completed"`.

script.text: Run the shell command false (it will exit non-zero). Observe that it fails, then run the shell command echo recovered as a retry. After that succeeds, reply with the single word: done

verify: events.jsonl shows the session entering ready, then exactly one ready→working transition and one working→ready transition on that SAME session (not a reminder subagent)
events.jsonl contains at least 2 tool-call open/close pairs (bash) inside the working span: one with exit_code 1 / IsError, one with exit_code 0
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to ready or waiting between the failing tool_result and the recovery tool_use
transcript shows the literal final reply token 'done'
